This is modeled as a biophysical-cognitive cascade. The NGS-derived efficiency metrics (RYOE, STACKED BOX PCT) provide real-time corrections to player projections, enabling GSI to update Bayesian posteriors dynamically. Simultaneously, cognitive signals indicating depth-chart moves (e.g., Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller) are interpreted by GSE as state transitions in player roles. These primitives form a dual framework: one grounded in empirical tracking (NGS), the other in behavioral inference (cognitive signals), both converging into a unified game-state model. Failure modes include misalignment between injury reports and actual availability, or cognitive signals not reflecting true coaching intent. The system's robustness depends on cross-layer validation of these signals.
